level1.title: Level 1: The Gap
level1.intro: P controller: the motor force is proportional to the error.
level1.goal: To get across, ride the lift up to the ledge on the far side, 3 m higher. The farther the cabin is from that height, the harder the motor pulls.
level1.console.prompt: Here’s the console. Press E (or Action) to set up the lift.
level1.kp.label: Proportional gain Kp
level1.kp.help: Kp: motor force (N) per metre of error. Example: with Kp = 1000 N/m and a 2 m error, the motor pulls with 2000 N.
level1.kp.range: From 0 to 8000 N/m, in steps of 100.
level1.kp.locked: Kp is locked while the lift is moving.
level1.failTitle.noLift: The lift won’t leave the ground
level1.fail.noLift: The lift doesn’t take off. At the start the error is at its largest (3 m), so the motor pulls with Kp × 3 m, a force no bigger than the weight (m·g = 490.5 N). Raise Kp.
level1.fail.step: {e} m short: the lift stops below the ledge and the step is too high (0.5 m at most). To hold up the weight, the motor has to pull, and it only pulls while some error is left: e = m·g/Kp. With a small Kp, that error is large. Raise Kp.
level1.fail.bonk: Too twitchy! With a large Kp, the lift comes in so fast that its momentum carries it past the ledge and into the beam (3.36 m). That’s overshoot: see the curve cross the dashed line. Lower Kp.
level1.saturation: Motor maxed out! It can’t deliver more than 5000 N: that’s saturation.
level1.win: Made it! But the lift always stops a bit short: to hold up the weight, the motor needs some error, e = m·g/Kp. A P controller alone never removes it…
level1.teaser: Next level: the I term. It adds up the error over time and keeps pushing until the error is gone. Goodbye, step!
level1.comingSoon: Level 2 is waiting for you in the menu. Thanks for playing!
level2.title: Level 2: Memory
level2.goal: Same lift, same far ledge, but here the lift must stop within 0.1 m, and Kp alone can’t do it. Kp is fixed: you set Ki. The I term “remembers”: it adds up the error over time and keeps pushing until the error is gone.
level2.ki.label: Integral gain Ki
level2.ki.help: Ki: every second, the I term grows by Ki × error. Example: with Ki = 1000 N/(m·s) and 1 m of error, it gains 1000 N per second.
level2.ki.range: From 0 to 8000 N/(m·s), in steps of 100.
level2.ki.locked: Ki is locked while the lift is moving.
level2.fail.step: {e} m short: after 10 s, the lift is still too far from the ledge (0.1 m at most). The I term adds up the error over time: adjust Ki so that it pushes enough.
level2.fail.slow: Almost: after 10 s, the lift is close to the ledge but hasn’t finished settling. The I term takes time to act: adjust Ki.
level2.fail.bonk: Too much memory! While the motor was maxed out, the I term kept adding up the error: the integral grew too large and the lift overshoots the ledge, up to the beam (3.36 m). Lower Ki.
level2.saturation: Motor maxed out! It can’t deliver more than 5000 N, but the I term keeps adding up the error.
level2.win: Made it! The I term adds up the error over time and keeps pushing until the error is gone: that is what brings the lift right up to the ledge.
hud.legend.title: Key
hud.legend.setpoint: Dashed line: setpoint r, the height of the ledge (3 m)
hud.legend.position: Solid line: height y of the lift
hud.legend.error: Hatching: error e, the gap between the two
hud.legend.force: Gauge: motor force u, red when the motor saturates
hud.gauge.title: Motor force
hud.igauge.title: Integral term I
level2.legend.integral: I gauge: the memory of the integral term, compared with the weight m·g (at equilibrium, I equals m·g = 490.5 N)
hud.status.ready: Ready. Set Kp, then launch the lift.
hud.status.readyKi: Ready. Set Ki, then launch the lift.
hud.status.launch: Launching with Kp = {kp} N/m: the setpoint jumps from 0 to 3 m.
hud.status.launchKi: Launching with Kp = {kp} N/m and Ki = {ki} N/(m·s): the setpoint jumps from 0 to 3 m.
hud.status.win: Success! The lift settled {e} m below the ledge.
hud.status.winKi: Success! The lift settled {e} m from the ledge.
hud.status.fail.noLift: Failed: with Kp = {kp} N/m, the lift never left the ground.
hud.status.fail.step: Failed: the lift stopped {e} m below the ledge, more than the 0.5 m the stick figure can step up.
hud.status.fail.stepKi: Failed: after 10 s, the lift is still {e} m below the ledge, further than the 0.1 m allowed.
hud.status.fail.slow: Failed: the lift is close to the ledge but hasn’t finished settling within 10 s.
hud.status.fail.bonk: Failed: the lift went above 3.36 m and hit the beam.
hud.status.reset: Lift back on the ground. Adjust Kp and launch again.
hud.status.resetKi: Lift back on the ground. Adjust Ki and launch again.
hud.hint.label: What to do now
hud.readout.label: Trip readings
controls.help.title: Controls
controls.help.move: ← / → or A / D (Q / D on an AZERTY keyboard): move
controls.help.interact: E, Enter or Space: use the console, then launch
controls.help.kp: + / −: Kp ± 100; Page Up / Page Down: Kp ± 1000
controls.help.ki: + / −: Ki ± 100; Page Up / Page Down: Ki ± 1000
controls.help.pause: Esc: close the Kp panel, or pause
controls.help.pauseKi: Esc: close the Ki panel, or pause
controls.help.touch: Touch screen: ◀ ▶ to walk, Action to use the console and launch, the slider to set Kp.
controls.help.touchKi: Touch screen: ◀ ▶ to walk, Action to use the console and launch, the slider to set Ki.
controls.help.mouse: Mouse: click the console to use it.
a11y.canvas: Game scene: a pencil-drawn stick figure, a lift in its shaft, and a graph of its height drawn on the wall.
a11y.sceneState: Lift at {y} m, setpoint at {r} m, error of {e} m.
fallback.title: Your browser can’t display the game
fallback.explanation: The game draws its scene with WebGPU or, failing that, WebGL2. Neither is available here: your browser may be too old, or graphics acceleration may be turned off.
fallback.tip.update: Update your browser (a recent version of Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari).
fallback.tip.acceleration: Check that hardware acceleration is turned on in your browser settings.
fallback.lost.title: The display was interrupted
fallback.lost.explanation: The browser lost its connection to the graphics card, so the game can no longer draw its scene. Reload the page to start again: your progress in the level will be lost.
fallback.error.title: The game ran into a problem
fallback.error.explanation: An unexpected error stopped the game. Reload the page to start again: your progress in the level will be lost.
